templates_considered: audit_log_protected (RET-001): fit; used for the audit table and single-writer rule
audit_changes recipe: fit; used as the basis for the audit policy, but its per-statement rules were written by hand in AUDIT-001 and it does not carry a key of its own
ai_cost_and_agent_safety recipe: partial fit; its loop rule is used as AI-COST-001. Its VND-001, PERF-001, SEC-013 and CONV-030 templates were not added: the ask did not cover them
retained_data_cleaned_up (RET-002): did not fit; no retention ask
no_pii_in_responses, sensitive_fields_marked, tables_classified and other data templates: did not fit; the ask was about change tracking and AI spend

rules.covers: AI call inside a loop (the $900 incident)
only the audit function writes the audit log
creates of email tables are audited
edits of email tables are audited
patches of email tables are audited
deletes from email tables are audited

ask_parts_not_covered.part: spend cap on AI calls ($900 total, not just loops)
new tables that store emails are covered automatically
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: object.statement_required and table.write_location_restricted take exact table names only; no tag-based table selector was found for these rules

ask_parts_not_covered.part: who approved changes and who reads the audit log

assumptions: Customer-email tables are those with an email-typed or email-named field: customers, users, newsletter_subscribers, patients, orgs (billing_email), support_tickets (requester_email)
Actor is $auth.id where the endpoint requires login; null for public endpoints and for the summarizer and nightly task, which have no caller identity
A change is audited by the audit function call rather than by a database trigger, which the platform checks did not look at
retry_failed_webhooks is the task the customer means; its while loop is left unchanged
confusions: The recipe audit_changes lists per-statement object.statement_required rules but no key for the policy; I had to pick AUDIT-001 myself
The recipe for AI cost says 'AI calls are not made inside loops' and names ai.external.mcp.tool.run, but it is unclear whether that statement exists in every workspace
No example for when.tables with several tables; I assumed it accepts a list of table names
Unclear whether a db.add inside a loop counts as unconditional for placement; I treated any call inside a loop as not unconditional
The audit payload could leak fields such as password hashes depending on what is passed; the skill gives no guidance on what an audit payload should carry
wished_for: A tag-based table selector for object.statement_required (e.g. tables by tag), so a new table with emails is covered without editing the policy
A check for task retry caps or a loop exit guard
A recipe note on what an audit payload must not contain
Confirmation whether db.add counts as a write for the table.write_location_restricted statement list
why_confidence: The AI-in-loop rule is a direct fit and the audit single-writer rule is a template. The audit coverage depends on hand-listed table names and on every writer calling the function; writes that bypass it and new email tables are not caught. The retry-forever part is not covered at all.
